title: Health record
description: One durable fact per target per run, appended to `health/<slug>.jsonl` on the state branch (EDR-033). Append-only because shards run in parallel and a read-modify-write of one file from two shards loses records silently — appending is the only concurrency-safe operation available without a lock, and there are no locks by design (EDR-035). Every field earns its place by answering a question somebody asks during an incident.

adapter.description: Which code produced this — the first question asked in any incident.

pack_version.description: Which selector knowledge produced it. Packs are immutable, so this is answerable months later (SEL-01).

outcome.description: A record is written for EVERY outcome (HLTH-02). Writing only failures makes success rate — the primary health metric — uncomputable, because the denominator is gone.

published_count.description: Four counts rather than one: a drop between any adjacent pair localises the loss to a stage.

stop_reason.description: VAL-01: completeness is derived from THIS, never from the counts above. Both are recorded; only this one is authoritative.

stage_timings.description: Where the time went — and the input to the shard cost model, which balances by cost rather than by count (TR-CFG-004).

strategy_histogram.description: Which strategy index resolved each field. The EARLIEST upstream-change signal there is: a field that has always resolved at index 0 and starts resolving at index 1 says the source changed while the payload is still perfectly correct.
